title: upgrade: attention kernels -> flashattnv2 + fused ops + rope/rotary optimizations
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: reduce tail latency and token cost for medium-to-long sequences by replacing legacy attention paths with FlashAttentionV2-derived kernels, fusing rotary/rope ops where possible, and exposing a fused KV-cache-friendly codepath. This PR upgrades the runtime attention kernel selector to prefer fused FlashAttnV2 variants for supported model configs, adds a new ROPE/rotary fusion pass that removes redundant FFT-like transforms, and extends continuous-batching scheduler heuristics to be KV-cache aware. Changes include runtime kernel wrappers, kernel selection rules, microbench harnesses, and compatibility shims for legacy checkpoints. Benchmark summary: 1) 1.6-2.3x median throughput improvement on GPU A100/80 sequences >1024 tokens; 2) 15-30% reduction in p99 latency for interactive chat scenarios; 3) effective token cost reduction when batching small concurrent streams due to improved KV layout. Related Linear tasks: ENG-2481 ENG-2567 ENG-2642. This description includes implementation notes, tests, and rollout plan. Implementation notes: updated kernel registry with dynamic capability flags, added fallback to reference kernel for unsupported dtypes/seq lengths, and introduced a lightweight validation harness that runs microbenchmarks in CI for 4 representative model shapes. Testing & validation: unit tests for fused ops, integration test against model-registry smoke models, perf-canary runs in perf-canary cluster. Rollout: feature-flagged by default on main for canary runners, staged ramp to 25% traffic in Dedicated, and 100% after 1 week of canary metrics. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] perf harness - [x] feature flag - [x] migration notes for model-registry - [x] docs/notes for ops-team. Notes on compatibility: quantized kernels (4-bit/8-bit) use a different codepath and are not promoted to FlashAttnV2 in this change; separate follow-up planned (ENG-2704).
